contentEn:
Plumbing renovation is one of the most disruptive and technically complex renovation projects a Vancouver homeowner can undertake—involving behind-wall work that cannot be inspected after the fact, coordination with FortisBC for any gas line modifications, and compliance with the BC Building Code Part 7 as administered by the City of Vancouver—yet it is also one of the highest-ROI renovations, resolving water pressure problems, preventing water damage, and enabling bathroom and kitchen upgrades that would otherwise be impossible. A plumbing renovation in Vancouver costs $2,000 to $25,000 depending on scope in 2026: a simple fixture replacement runs $2,000 to $5,000, a bathroom plumbing renovation with new shower, toilet, and vanity runs $5,000 to $15,000, and a whole-house repipe for an older Vancouver character home runs $15,000 to $25,000. Reno Stars has been completing plumbing renovation projects across Vancouver, Burnaby, Richmond, and the North Shore since 2015, and Vancouver homeowners should understand that the City of Vancouver requires a plumbing permit for any work beyond simple fixture swaps, that FortisBC must be contacted before any work on gas lines, and that the BC Building Code Part 7 sets minimum pipe sizing, slope, and venting requirements that differ significantly from older Vancouver installation standards.

Vancouver Plumbing Renovation Permit Requirements

Understanding when a plumbing permit is required in Vancouver is the first step in any plumbing renovation:

  • A Vancouver plumbing permit is required for any work that adds, removes, or alters any part of the drain, waste, or vent (DWV) system; any work that adds or modifies a water service; any work on a backflow prevention device; and any gas line installation or modification. A plumbing permit is NOT required for simple fixture swaps where the drain connections do not change—such as replacing an existing toilet or faucet with a new one of the same type.
  • Plumbing permits in Vancouver are administered by the City of Vancouver's building department. Applications must include detailed drawings showing the proposed layout, pipe sizing, and connection points. For complex renovations involving structural changes or multiple fixtures, a registered plumbing engineer or certified plumber must prepare the drawings. Permit fees in Vancouver are calculated based on the number of fixtures being added or modified, typically ranging from $200 to $1,500 per fixture group.
  • FortisBC must be contacted before any work on gas lines in Vancouver—including water heater replacements, furnace connections, gas fireplace installations, and any extension of gas lines to new appliances. All gas work in Vancouver must be performed by a registered gas contractor with a valid FortisBC permit. Working on a gas line without a FortisBC permit is a serious safety violation and may void your home insurance coverage.
  • BC Building Code Part 7 governs plumbing installations in BC, including Vancouver. Part 7 sets minimum pipe sizing requirements (typically 1.25-inch minimum for supply lines and 1.5-inch minimum for branch drains in Vancouver residential installations), minimum slopes for drain pipes (1/4 inch per foot minimum for 1.5-inch to 3-inch pipes), and detailed venting requirements that must be met for the system to drain properly. Many older Vancouver homes have plumbing that does not meet current Part 7 requirements, and a renovation that touches the plumbing system may trigger an upgrade requirement.
  • Backflow prevention requirements in Vancouver: Any renovation that modifies a cross-connection in the water supply system—including adding a dishwasher, washing machine, or irrigation system—requires a backflow prevention device at the point of connection. The type of device required depends on the degree of hazard, and the installation must be inspected by the City of Vancouver.
  • Water service replacement in Vancouver: If the water service line from the street to the home is old (many Vancouver homes have lead or galvanized steel service lines from the 1950s and earlier), a plumbing renovation may trigger a requirement to replace the entire service line. This requires coordination with the City of Vancouver's engineering department and a separate permit. Water service replacement in Vancouver typically costs $5,000 to $15,000 depending on the distance from the main to the home.

Frequently Asked Questions About Plumbing Renovation in Vancouver

Do I need a permit for plumbing renovation in Vancouver?

You need a Vancouver plumbing permit for any work that adds, removes, or alters the drain, waste, or vent system, modifies the water service, or involves any gas line work. Simple fixture swaps—like replacing a toilet or faucet with a similar model where the drain connection does not change—do not require a permit in Vancouver. But if you are moving a sink, adding a bathroom, installing a dishwasher, replacing a water heater, or doing any work on a gas line, you need a permit. A Vancouver building permit for a typical bathroom plumbing renovation costs $500 to $3,000 depending on the number of fixtures and whether it is processed as a standalone plumbing permit or part of a larger renovation permit. Gas work additionally requires a FortisBC permit, which your registered gas contractor obtains as part of the work. Working without a required permit in Vancouver can result in a stop-work order, a fine, and complications when you sell the home.

How much does a whole-house repipe cost in Vancouver?

A whole-house repipe in Vancouver costs $15,000 to $25,000 depending on the size of the home, the type of pipe selected, and the accessibility of the existing plumbing. This project is typically needed for Vancouver homes built before 1970 that still have galvanized steel supply pipes—a material that corrodes internally over time, causing low water pressure, rust-coloured water, and increased risk of leaks. The cost includes removing the old galvanized pipes, installing new copper or PEX supply lines, reconnecting all fixtures, and pressure testing the system to BC Building Code Part 7 standards. PEX (cross-linked polyethylene) pipe is increasingly preferred in Vancouver renovations because it costs 20–30% less than copper, installs faster with fewer joints, and is more resistant to freeze damage in Vancouver's occasional cold winters. The project takes 1–3 weeks depending on home size and whether the walls are opened during a larger renovation. Vancouver homeowners should also budget $500–$1,500 for any required drywall repair and painting after the repipe is complete.

What is involved in replacing a water heater in Vancouver?

Replacing a water heater in Vancouver involves selecting a new unit, obtaining a FortisBC permit for gas-connected units, and having the work performed by a registered gas contractor (for gas units) or a licensed plumber. A standard 40–50 gallon tank water heater in Vancouver costs $2,500 to $6,000 installed, including the unit, labour, removal of the old tank, and the FortisBC permit. A tankless on-demand water heater in Vancouver costs $5,000 to $12,000 installed but has a longer lifespan (20–25 years versus 10–15 for tanks) and lower operating costs due to higher efficiency. FortisBC offers rebates on tankless water heaters through its Conservation and Energy Optimization programs—check the current FortisBC website for 2026 rebate amounts, which typically range from $500 to $2,000 depending on the unit efficiency rating. The City of Vancouver requires that the new water heater be installed to BC Building Code Part 7 standards, including proper venting, gas line sizing, and T&P valve installation. An improperly installed water heater in Vancouver can create a carbon monoxide hazard if the venting is not correct—a critical safety issue in Vancouver's tightly sealed homes.

  • 温哥华的管道许可证由温哥华市建筑部门管理。申请必须包括显示拟议布局、管道尺寸和连接点的详细图纸。对于涉及结构更改或多个设备的复杂装修，注册管道工程师或认证水管工必须准备图纸。温哥华的许可证费用根据添加或修改的设备数量计算，通常为每个设备组$200至$1,500。
  • 在进行温哥华任何煤气管道工程之前（包括热水器更换、炉子连接、煤气壁炉安装及任何将煤气管道延伸至新设备），必须联系FortisBC。所有温哥华煤气工程必须由持有有效FortisBC许可证的注册煤气承包商进行。在没有FortisBC许可证的情况下操作煤气管道是严重的安全违规行为，可能使您的房屋保险失效。

  • 温哥华防回流要求：任何修改供水系统中交叉连接的装修——包括添加洗碗机、洗衣机或灌溉系统——需要在连接点安装防回流装置。所需装置类型取决于危险程度，安装必须由温哥华市进行检查。
  • 温哥华供水服务更换：如果从街道到房屋的供水服务线路老化（许多温哥华房屋有1950年代及更早的铅或镀锌钢管服务线路），管道装修可能会触发更换整个服务线路的要求。这需要与温哥华市工程部门协调和单独许可证。温哥华供水服务更换通常费用为$5,000至$15,000，取决于从主管到房屋的距离。

关于温哥华管道装修的常见问题

温哥华管道装修需要许可证吗？

您需要对任何添加、移除或改动排水、废物或排气系统、修改供水服务或涉及任何煤气管道工程的工程申请温哥华管道许可证。简单的设备更换——如更换为相同型号的马桶或水龙头，排水连接不变——在温哥华不需要许可证。但如果您要移动水槽、添加浴室、安装洗碗机、更换热水器或进行任何煤气管道工程，则需要许可证。典型浴室管道装修的温哥华建筑许可证费用为$500至$3,000，取决于设备数量及是作为独立管道许可证还是作为较大型装修许可证的一部分处理。煤气工程还需要FortisBC许可证，由您的注册煤气承包商作为工程的一部分获取。在温哥华无所需许可证施工可能导致停工令、罚款及售房时的复杂情况。

温哥华全屋重管道费用是多少？

温哥华全屋重管道费用为$15,000至$25,000，取决于房屋大小、所选管道类型及现有管道的可及性。此项目通常适用于1970年前建造、仍使用镀锌钢供应管道的温哥华房屋——这种材料会随着时间内部腐蚀，导致水压低、水呈铁锈色及漏水风险增加。费用包括拆除旧镀锌管道、安装新铜或PEX供应管道、重新连接所有设备，并按BC建筑规范第7部分标准对系统进行压力测试。PEX（交联聚乙烯）管道在温哥华装修中越来越受欢迎，因为它比铜便宜20-30%，安装更快、接头更少，且更能抵抗温哥华偶尔寒冬的冻害。该项目需要1至3周，取决于房屋大小以及是否在较大装修期间打开墙壁。温哥华业主还应预算$500至$1,500用于重管道完成后所需的任何干墙修复和油漆。

温哥华更换热水器涉及什么？

温哥华更换热水器涉及选择新设备、为煤气连接设备获取FortisBC许可证，并由注册煤气承包商（煤气设备）或持证水管工进行工作。温哥华标准40-50加仑储水式热水器含设备、人工、旧罐拆除和FortisBC许可证的安装费用为$2,500至$6,000。温哥华即热式热水器含安装费用为$5,000至$12,000，但使用寿命更长（20-25年vs储水式的10-15年），且由于更高效率而运营成本更低。FortisBC通过其节能优化计划为即热式热水器提供补贴——请查看当前FortisBC网站了解2026年补贴金额，通常为$500至$2,000，取决于设备效率等级。温哥华市要求新热水器按BC建筑规范第7部分标准安装，包括正确的排气、煤气管道尺寸和T&P阀安装。如果排气不正确，温哥华安装不当的热水器可能产生一氧化碳危险——这是温哥华密封房屋中的关键安全问题。
